statement: Define foreign exchange as FEMA, 1999 does, and describe how the foreign exchange market is organised and who takes part in it
Read exchange rate quotations: direct and indirect quotes, two-way (bid and offer) quotes, and cash, tom, spot and forward value dates
Work out customer (merchant) rates, forward rates and cross rates from interbank quotes
Explain the factors that determine exchange rates and how the exchange rate mechanism works
Describe how a bank's foreign exchange dealing room operates and is controlled
Identify the derivative products used in foreign exchange business and what each is used for
Apply the RBI and FEDAI guidelines that govern foreign exchange dealings
Distinguish capital account and current account transactions and explain how the Foreign Exchange Management Act treats each
Apply the Liberalised Remittance Scheme: who is eligible, the annual limit, frequency, documents and how family and proprietors are treated
Identify the remittances that are permitted and those that are prohibited under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
source_caveats: Travel limits follow the RBI FAQ of 28 November 2025; the courseware may state different figures.

statement: Apply the operational conditions for capital account remittances and for gifts and loans to non-resident relatives under the scheme
source_caveats: The Overseas Investment Rules are taken from a secondary reproduction (2022 text); the Regulations and Directions (forms and timelines) were not retrieved and are not taught.

statement: Work out tax collected at source on remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
source_caveats: The statute says 'exceeding ten lakh rupees' without stating that the rate applies to the excess only; the items compute on the excess and say so in each stem.
The additional rate where PAN or Aadhaar is missing and TCS on transfers to an NRO account are not taught.

statement: State the reporting and other remittance facilities for residents that accompany the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
source_caveats: The reporting Master Direction (No. 18/2015-16) was not retrieved in substance (its RBI page lists only update history); reporting is taught as far as the LRS Master Direction states it (FETERS). The courseware's daily XBRL reporting is not taught.

statement: Explain what correspondent banking is, why banks need it, and which services depend on an account relationship
source_caveats: The FATF due-diligence statements for cross-border correspondent relationships are not used in items.

statement: Distinguish Nostro, Vostro, Loro and mirror accounts from the direction of the relationship, and reconcile a Nostro balance
Describe the electronic modes of transmission and payment systems used for cross-border and domestic funds transfer: SWIFT, CHIPS, Fedwire, CHAPS, TARGET, RTGS and NEFT
source_caveats: CHAPS settlement mode: courseware (net) and Bank of England (gross) disagree; taught as a flagged caution, not scored.

statement: Identify who is an NRI or PIO under FEMA and distinguish NRE, NRO, FCNR(B) and SNRR accounts by purpose, currency, deposit form, credits, debits and repatriability
source_caveats: Income-tax residency tests and RFC accounts for returning NRIs are not taught (no primary source checked).
Courseware and RBI differ on the NRE term and on where rent may be credited; no item tests those points.

statement: Apply the conditions for advances against non-resident deposits and for housing loans to NRIs
Describe the facilities available to NRIs for investing in India: shares and securities, funds, deposits, firms and immovable property
Define a documentary letter of credit and identify each party to it and what it does
Distinguish the types of letter of credit: irrevocable, confirmed, transferable, red and green clause, sight, usance, deferred payment, negotiation, back-to-back, standby and revolving
Trace the flow of an export letter of credit and an import letter of credit from application to payment
source_caveats: The credit flow is taught from the courseware (UCP 600 itself was not retrieved). EDPMS and IDPMS are taught under unit 5 (batch BFM-A-U05-B007).

statement: Apply the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600) and the liabilities, responsibilities and rights of the parties
source_caveats: UCP 600 itself was not retrieved; articles are taught from the courseware.

statement: Scrutinise documents under a credit, handle discrepancies, crystallise import bills and follow up bills
source_caveats: The substantive text of RBI's 16 January 2026 export-import directions (in force 1 October 2026) was not retrieved.

statement: Identify the risks in letter of credit transactions and the safeguards available to banks
Explain standby letters of credit and how they compare with guarantees
source_caveats: The Guarantees Regulations, 2026 do not mention standby letters of credit; the courseware's commercial standby safeguards for imports could not be verified and are withdrawn. ISP 98's articles are not taught (ICC publication not retrieved).

statement: Apply the Uniform Rules for Bank-to-Bank Reimbursements (URR 725)
source_caveats: URR 725's text was not retrieved; the 10-day and three-banking-day rules are taught as the courseware states them.

statement: Apply International Standard Banking Practice (ISBP 745) when examining documents
source_caveats: ISBP 745's own text was not retrieved; the courseware gives only its history and aims. The current edition is ISBP 821 (2023), which is mentioned but not taught.

statement: Apply the Incoterms 2020 rules to allocate cost, risk and delivery between buyer and seller
source_caveats: Incoterms 2020's rule texts were not retrieved; rule lists and allocations are taught from the trade administration page and the courseware matrix, which omits DAP.

statement: Distinguish the exchange control and trade control frameworks that govern exports and imports, and the roles of RBI, DGFT, FEDAI and ICC
Apply the export declaration, documentation, time limit and payment rules for exporters
source_caveats: Export Regulations text is the RBI page with its footnotes; the January 2026 export and import directions (in force 1 October 2026, after the cut-off) are not taught; the Master Direction paragraph on rupee settlement was substituted on 17 July 2026 and only the account mechanics are taught.

statement: Apply the facilities connected with exports: agency commission, reduction in invoice value, claims, refund, extension of time, write-off and foreign currency accounts
source_caveats: The FEDAI effective date of realisation is taught under FEDAI Rules (batch BFM-A-U01-B009), not repeated here.

statement: Explain export finance: pre-shipment and post-shipment credit, and the Gold Card scheme for exporters
source_caveats: The page of RBI's Credit Facilities Directions saved is the version of 1 October 2026; earlier versions of Chapter XV were not retrieved.
Time-limited Trade Relief Measures directions are not taught; the Normal Transit Period and crystallisation come from FEDAI Rules (batch BFM-A-U01-B009).

statement: Describe the Export Data Processing and Monitoring System and the follow-up of export bills
Explain factoring and forfaiting and when each is used
source_caveats: The courseware gives LIBOR-based discount examples; the rules taught here come from the RBI Master Direction.

statement: Apply the exchange and trade control guidelines for importers, including advance remittance, time limits and evidence of import
source_caveats: The January 2026 import directions, in force from 1 October 2026, are not taught.

statement: Explain import finance and the Import Data Processing and Monitoring System
Distinguish supplier's credit from buyer's credit and describe the rules on trade credit
source_caveats: Trade credit figures come from the 2018 Regulations page as updated 16 February 2026; not re-checked against a consolidated 2026 text.

statement: Apply the guidelines to a case on export finance
source_caveats: The case uses assumed bank terms and a stated normal transit period; the period is from FEDAI Rules (batch BFM-A-U01-B009).

statement: Identify who may borrow and lend under the external commercial borrowing framework, the currency and forms of borrowing, and the borrowing limit
source_caveats: The courseware describes the earlier framework; if the examination follows it, older figures may be tested and are not taught.

statement: Apply the rules on maturity, cost of borrowing and end-use restrictions for external commercial borrowings
source_caveats: The maturity computation annex was not read; the trade credit spread is not tested because the regulation text and the courseware differ.

statement: Apply the operational rules for external commercial borrowings: receipt of proceeds, security, refinancing, change of terms and debt servicing
source_caveats: The Master Direction on ECBs, Trade Credits and Structured Obligations was not retrieved.

statement: Meet the reporting requirements for external commercial borrowings and explain conversion of a borrowing into equity
Explain foreign direct investment and foreign portfolio investment: key concepts, eligible investors and investees, instruments and prohibited sectors
Apply the operational rules for foreign investment: transfers, pledge of shares and reporting
Classify the risks in international trade and the ways to manage them
Apply the Reserve Bank guidelines on country risk exposure and the ECGC country risk classification
source_caveats: Country risk provisioning percentages (in the 2025 Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions) are not taught; the RBI Concentration Risk Management Directions copy is updated to 1 October 2026, after the cut-off.

statement: Explain the origin, role and regulatory position of ECGC and the principle of risk sharing
Describe the ECGC policies for exporters and what they cover and exclude
source_caveats: Only the Shipment Comprehensive Risks sheet was read from ECGC; other policy terms (small exporter limit, protracted default period, percentages) are from the courseware, which predates current ECGC literature.

statement: Describe the ECGC covers for banks, the guarantees and special schemes, and the obligations and claims procedure
source_caveats: Cover percentages, premiums and claim periods for bank covers are from the courseware; the ECIB sales literature could not be read as text and those figures are not tested.

statement: Describe the role, functions and products of EXIM Bank
source_caveats: EXIM Bank content is from the courseware only; no EXIM Bank or Government document was read.

statement: Explain the Reserve Bank's powers under FEMA over authorised dealers and the returns they file
source_caveats: The list of returns is from the courseware and was not checked against the Reserve Bank's current list.

statement: Explain the objective and legal character of FEMA and apply the Current Account Transactions Rules
source_caveats: The Current Account Transactions Rules copy is updated only to 26 May 2015; later amendments were not searched for. The courseware's account of ODI, RFC and RFC(D) accounts is not taught here.

statement: Describe the formation and functions of FEDAI
Explain ADRs, GDRs, FCCBs and FCEBs
source_caveats: ADR and GDR content is general market description from the courseware; the Depository Receipts Scheme was not read. The courseware's FCCB and FCEB conditions belong to the earlier framework and are not taught.

statement: Explain what an international financial services centre is and why GIFT City was set up
source_caveats: GIFT City start date, company counts and the tax exemption are the courseware's statements; the SEZ Act and Income-tax provisions were not read.

statement: Describe the role of the International Financial Services Centres Authority
Apply the licensing and capital requirements for a banking unit in an IFSC
source_caveats: The Regulations text is the consolidation as amended up to 14 July 2023; later amendments were not searched for. The courseware says licensing needs Reserve Bank permission; the Regulations name the IFSCA.

statement: Apply the prudential requirements for an IFSC banking unit
source_caveats: The IFSCA directions on reserve ratios, exposure norms and the specified liquidity ratios were not retrieved; the courseware's 3 per cent reserve ratio and 5/10 per cent exposure ceilings are not tested as current.

statement: State the business an IFSC banking unit may and may not do, and the relaxations for foreign portfolio investors
source_caveats: FPI tax relaxations at GIFT City are the courseware's account and were not checked against the Income-tax Act.

statement: Trace the evolution of technology in banking and weigh its benefits and limits
source_caveats: Content is the courseware's account; no external source was read.

statement: Describe the digital platforms used in international banking and the Reserve Bank monitoring systems
source_caveats: EDPMS and IDPMS mechanics and the eBRC date are checked against the Reserve Bank Master Directions; the courseware's EDPMS and FIRMS dates were not verified.

statement: Explain how fintech, artificial intelligence, big data and robotic process automation are used
source_caveats: Content is the courseware's account; dated fintech statistics are not taught.

statement: Explain how blockchain changes a documentary credit and its advantages
source_caveats: The blockchain credit flow is the courseware's illustrative description.

statement: State the challenges of fintech and blockchain and the developments in India
source_caveats: Statements about Indian Block Chain Infrastructure Co. Pvt Ltd and IDRBT's phased adoption are the courseware's and were not verified.

statement: Define risk, uncertainty and financial risk and relate risk to the variability of cash flow
source_caveats: Conceptual content is the courseware's account; no external source was read.

statement: Explain the linkage among risk, capital and return, including the risk premium and risk adjusted return
source_caveats: RAROC is taught as a concept; the courseware gives no formula.

statement: Explain why risk needs to be managed and describe the organisation for risk management
source_caveats: Organisation of risk committees is the courseware's description of usual practice; Reserve Bank guidance on risk governance was not read.

statement: Identify risks in a transaction and apply sensitivity, volatility and downside potential measures
source_caveats: Measurement concepts are the courseware's account; Reserve Bank guidance on value at risk was not read here.

statement: Apply risk pricing and the Reserve Bank rules on lending rates
source_caveats: Lending rate rules checked against the 28 November 2025 Interest Rates on Advances Directions; later amendments were not compared. Risk pricing components are the courseware's.

statement: Describe risk monitoring, mitigation, diversification and enterprise-wide risk management
source_caveats: CCIL role and the COSO framework are the courseware's statements and were not verified.

statement: Describe the business lines of banking and the grouping of exposures into banking book, trading book and off-balance sheet exposures
source_caveats: Business lines follow the Basel table as reproduced in the courseware; the Basel text was not read.

statement: Describe the characteristics of the banking book and the risks it carries
source_caveats: Conceptual content is the courseware's account.

statement: Describe the characteristics of the trading book and the risks it carries, and how investments are now classified
source_caveats: The courseware's 90-day holding statement for Held for Trading reflects older practice and is not tested; classification follows the 28 November 2025 Directions (copy updated to 1 October 2026, after the cut-off).

statement: Describe off-balance sheet exposures and the risks they carry
source_caveats: Conceptual content is the courseware's account.

statement: Define liquidity risk and distinguish funding, time and call risk
source_caveats: Definitions are the courseware's account.

statement: Define interest rate risk and distinguish gap, basis, yield curve, embedded option, reinvestment and net interest position risk
source_caveats: Definitions are the courseware's account.

statement: Define market, credit, operational and model risk and their sub-types
source_caveats: Definitions are the courseware's account; the Basel Committee definition of operational risk was not read in its source.

statement: Explain climate risk: physical and transition risks
source_caveats: Physical and transition risk rest on the courseware's general description; the Reserve Bank Directions read contain only the green deposits framework, and their copy is marked updated after the cut-off.

statement: Explain why banking is regulated, the goals of regulation and systemic risk
source_caveats: Content is the courseware's account of regulatory goals; no source beyond it was read.

statement: Describe the Bank for International Settlements and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision
source_caveats: BIS and BCBS facts are the courseware's; the Basel Committee's own pages were not read.

statement: Explain the 1988 Basel Accord, the risk weight buckets and the Cooke ratio
source_caveats: Basel I details are the courseware's account, consistent with the standard text; the 1988 Accord itself was not read.

statement: Explain the 1996 amendment for market risk and the reasons for revising Basel I
source_caveats: The 1996 amendment parameters are the courseware's account; the BCBS document was not read.

statement: Describe the three pillars and approaches of Basel II
source_caveats: Basel II details are the courseware's account; the BCBS framework was not read. Indian banks use the Basic Indicator Approach for operational risk under the 2025 Directions.

statement: Explain the origin and innovations of Basel III and the Indian minimum capital ratios
source_caveats: The Directions copy is updated to 7 October 2026, after the cut-off; the courseware's phase-in dates and circular references were not checked against the circulars.

statement: Apply the standardised approach capital charge for credit risk and external credit assessments
source_caveats: Standard cases only; the Directions copy is updated to 7 October 2026 (after the cut-off) and later amendments were not compared. Housing risk weights taught for loans sanctioned on or after 7 June 2017; other windows not read. The courseware's agency list differs from the Directions' table.

statement: Apply credit risk mitigation techniques and their capital treatment
source_caveats: Standard cases only; haircut tables and further CRM categories are not taught. Basel text not read.

statement: Apply the capital charge for market risk
source_caveats: The courseware's equity charge (9 plus 9) differs from the 2025 Directions (11.25 plus 9); the Directions are taught. Option charges, specific risk tables for bank and corporate bonds and securitisation are not taught.

statement: Apply the capital charge for operational risk
source_caveats: The courseware's account of the proposed standardised measurement approach is not tested; the Directions encourage readiness for a new standardised approach.

statement: Describe Pillar 2 supervisory review and Pillar 3 market discipline
source_caveats: Directions copy updated to 7 October 2026 (after the cut-off); ICAAP annexure and Pillar 3 templates beyond DF-2 to DF-4 were not read.

statement: Explain the capital conservation buffer, leverage ratio, countercyclical buffer and systemically important banks
source_caveats: Directions copy updated to 7 October 2026 (after the cut-off); the courseware's D-SIB list (March 2018 data) and its statement that the countercyclical buffer has been zero since 2015 were not verified and are not tested.

statement: Describe risk based supervision
source_caveats: Risk based supervision is the courseware's account only; no Reserve Bank document on current supervisory practice or ratings was read.

statement: Identify the elements of CET1, Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital, minority interest and the regulatory deductions
source_caveats: Capital elements and deductions checked against the Directions (paragraphs 12, 27, 28); amendments after the cut-off were not separated; courseware's AFS and quarterly profit statements are older.

statement: Apply credit conversion factors to off-balance sheet items and explain counterparty credit risk terms
source_caveats: CCFs match the Directions; add-on factors taken from the Directions as substituted from 10 March 2026, not the courseware's older table.

statement: Apply eligible collateral, haircuts and the stepwise computation of risk-weighted assets for credit risk
source_caveats: Ratings, collateral and haircuts checked against the Directions; courseware's risk weight list by exposure type and guarantor weights are not verified; enclosures after printed p. 388 read in part.

statement: Explain market risk, trading liquidity risk and credit and counterparty risk in the trading book
source_caveats: Conceptual content is the courseware's account; the statements on commodities in the trading book and on RTGS and CCIL were not verified.

statement: Describe the market risk management framework, its organisation and risk identification
source_caveats: Organisation and product programme descriptions are the courseware's account of usual practice; Reserve Bank guidance was not checked.

statement: Apply basis point value, duration and modified duration
source_caveats: Standard finance concepts, recomputed in tests; no external source read.

statement: Explain and apply value at risk, its methods and limitations
source_caveats: Courseware account with standard z-values; no external source read.

statement: Explain back testing and stress testing
source_caveats: Courseware account; the BIS January 1996 back testing paper was not read.

statement: Describe monitoring and control, reporting, management of trading liquidity and market risk mitigation
source_caveats: Courseware account of controls and mitigation; no external source read.

statement: Explain credit risk, its components and the credit risk management framework and organisation
source_caveats: Directions copy updated to 1 October 2026 includes amendments after the cut-off; the Guidance Note on Credit Risk Management was not read.

statement: Distinguish default risk, downgrade risk, concentration risk, systematic risk, counterparty risk and country risk
source_caveats: Conceptual content is the courseware's account.

statement: Explain credit rating, rating migration, expected and unexpected loss and credit risk models
source_caveats: Rating, migration and the named models (CreditMetrics, CreditRisk+, Altman Z) are the courseware's account; no source read for them.

statement: Describe credit risk control and monitoring at transaction level: approval, appraisal, limits and risk pricing
source_caveats: Transaction level controls are the courseware's account of good practice; the Guidance Note was not read.

statement: Describe credit control and monitoring at portfolio level, active portfolio management and the loan review mechanism
source_caveats: Portfolio and loan review practice is the courseware's account (including the 30-40 per cent review sample); the Guidance Note was not read.

statement: Explain securitisation and the Reserve Bank's minimum retention requirement
source_caveats: Minimum retention figures checked against the 2025 Securitisation Directions; the courseware's 2021 Master Direction reference is not used.

statement: Explain credit derivatives: credit default swaps, total return swaps, credit linked notes and credit spread options
source_caveats: The courseware describes the 2022 credit derivatives framework, superseded on 25 June 2026; the 2026 text was read only through a website reproduction; ISDA credit events and product descriptions are the courseware's.

statement: Apply the credit risk techniques in the additional reading: the Altman Z score, the default probability implied by interest rates, exposure after collateral haircuts and the rating transition matrix
source_caveats: Courseware printed pp. 452-454 (additional reading); no external source on the Altman Z model was read, so its coefficients, the 1.81 cut-off and the definition of X4 are the courseware's.

The courseware's collateral illustration applies a 9 per cent exposure haircut to loans (E* = 87 crore); the 2025 Capital Adequacy Directions (paragraphs 161 to 163) give loans no exposure haircut, so the lesson teaches the Directions and states the courseware variant.
The courseware's default probability example (3 per cent) is rounded; unrounded 3.11 per cent. The no-recovery assumption is the author's reading of the formula.
Reviewer is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.

statement: Define operational risk, its nature and the cause, effect and event based classifications
source_caveats: Basel definition, event types and cause classification are the courseware's account; Basel texts were not read.

statement: State the Basel principles for the sound management of operational risk
source_caveats: The eleven Basel principles (2011) are the courseware's account; the Basel text was not read.

statement: Describe the organisation, processes and monitoring of operational risk management
source_caveats: Organisation and process description is the courseware's; the Reserve Bank's operational risk guidance note was not read.

statement: Apply the basic indicator, standardised and advanced measurement approaches and the generic risk estimate
source_caveats: Basic Indicator Approach checked against the Capital Adequacy Directions; betas for the Standardised Approach and the AMA are the courseware's account.

statement: Describe the parameters of the advanced measurement approach and operational risk mitigation
source_caveats: AMA parameters, CORDEx details and the generic risk formula are the courseware's account; the AMA is not used by banks in India.

statement: Explain the new Basel III standardised approach for operational risk in the Reserve Bank's Directions
source_caveats: Basel III Standardised Approach read from the Forthcoming Instructions Directions; no effective date was found; the courseware's loss threshold and 100 per cent rule could not be matched.

statement: Explain integrated risk management: need, challenges and approach
source_caveats: The April 2017 Reserve Bank advice on the Chief Risk Officer is the courseware's statement and was not checked against a primary text.

statement: Define liquidity and liquidity risk, its types, drivers and importance
source_caveats: Concepts, types and drivers from the courseware, consistent with the Directions' introduction.

statement: State the Basel principles for sound liquidity risk management
source_caveats: Principles taught from Annex IV of the Directions; the Basel Committee text was not read.

statement: Describe governance, policy, tolerance and strategy for liquidity risk management
source_caveats: Governance, tolerance and policy checked against the Directions (Chapters II and III).

statement: Measure liquidity risk with the flow approach, structural liquidity statement and stock ratios
source_caveats: Mismatch limits and ratio definitions checked against the Directions; courseware's industry averages are not tested.

statement: Describe stress testing, contingency funding, management information and internal controls
source_caveats: Stress periods, contingency plan and controls checked against the Directions; return submission time lags were not checked.

statement: Apply the norms for overseas operations, foreign currency liquidity and Reserve Bank reporting
source_caveats: Overseas norms and reporting periodicity checked against the Directions; the Filing of Supervisory Returns Directions were not read.

statement: Explain the purpose of the Basel III liquidity standards and how they fit with the other Basel III measures
source_caveats: Basel III context is the courseware's account, including its statement on the capital adequacy ratio.

statement: Define the Liquidity Coverage Ratio, its minimum, scope and stress scenario
source_caveats: Checked against the Directions; courseware phase-in and pandemic relaxation are historical and not tested.

statement: Classify high quality liquid assets and compute the stock of HQLA with haircuts and caps
source_caveats: Checked against the Directions; FALLCR percentage differs from the courseware (Directions used); 1 April 2026 changes taken from the Directions only.

statement: Compute total net cash outflows and the Liquidity Coverage Ratio
source_caveats: Retail run-off rates and the inflow cap come from the Directions; other run-off and inflow rates are not taught.

source_caveats: Monitoring tools and returns checked against the Directions; submission time limits not tested.

source_caveats: ASF and RSF factors checked against the Directions; NSFR effective dates are the courseware's account.
